claims.text: As-cast HfNbTaTiZr contains inherent lattice distortions at room temperature.
The room-temperature microstructure and mechanical behavior of HfNbTaTiZr have been characterized.
In situ diffraction during elevated-temperature uniaxial loading can track lattice-strain and elastic responses.
TEM or digital image correlation can monitor dislocation activity or dislocation density sufficiently to distinguish it from lattice-distortion relaxation.
Increasing temperature thermally activates relaxation of inherent lattice distortions in HfNbTaTiZr.
Relaxation of the lattice distortions increases interatomic spacing.
The increased interatomic spacing directly lowers the elastic modulus.
Lattice-distortion relaxation modifies the stress–strain behavior of HfNbTaTiZr.
Lattice-distortion relaxation affects the thermal expansion of HfNbTaTiZr.
Above approximately 600°C, HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit measurable lattice-parameter shifts and reduced diffraction-peak broadening.
Reduced diffraction-peak broadening above approximately 600°C indicates relaxation of lattice distortions.
The predicted structural changes above approximately 600°C will correlate with a lower elastic modulus and deviations of the stress–strain curves from their room-temperature behavior.
Room-temperature lattice distortion, elastic modulus, and thermal-expansion measurements are available as the control state.
Above about 1000°C, phase transformations or competing mechanisms may confound the proposed lattice-relaxation response.
Thermally activated dislocation activity may occur concurrently with lattice-distortion relaxation and confound attribution of the response.
